_comment: Which families a board actually runs. Getting this wrong writes one firmware at a board expecting another - a cartographer probe flashed with upstream klipper, or judged against a source tree it was never built from - so every step from reading the key to acting on it is guarded.

mutations.name: families() returns exactly what a type declares
the declared firmware list is kept, not discarded on load
a family nobody declared is refused rather than accepted

mutations._comment: Raising on the first undeclared family made a config with two typos take two reloads to fix. validate collects every miss and raises once.
mutations.name: every undeclared family is reported at once, not just the first
mutations.replace: raise ConfigCorruptError(f"{fw}", path=path, type=entry.name, value=fw, missing={entry.name: [fw]})

mutations._comment: load() now refuses a type with no firmware: key at all (step 11), so _save() cannot leave it implicit even for the plain-klipper case any more - it is always written, never omitted as a restated default.
mutations.name: the declared firmware list is always written back on save
the application is the first declared family that is not a bootloader
the bootloader is the first declared family that is one
a type's families keep their declared order
mutations.find: declared = [fw for fw in self.firmwares if fw in self.fws]
mutations.replace: declared = sorted(fw for fw in self.firmwares if fw in self.fws)

mutations.name: add_type refuses a family it assembled that nobody declared

mutations._comment: I2: type_update's katapult_installed branch set mcu.firmwares without checking the family was declared, saving a config the next Registry.load refused - taking every type down with it. _save() now revalidates the document it is about to write with the same check load() applies, before any byte reaches disk.
mutations.name: _save() refuses a document typelist.validate would refuse
